requirements.requirement: Keep /srv/data recoverable through a functioning filesystem-snapshot mechanism.
requirements.summary: A valid rsnapshot configuration targets /srv/data, stores snapshots under /srv/snapshots, and retains seven daily generations. Multiple snapshots were directly inspected, and a new snapshot completed successfully after the final reboot.

requirements.requirement: After /srv/data is modified, restore the exact content captured by an earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: The captured snapshot exactly matched the original manifest; subsequent changes altered content, permissions, file presence, and a symlink; restoration reproduced the original SHA-256 manifest, content, metadata, and symlink while removing the added file. The restored state remained intact after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations show Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts unchanged. rsnapshot 1.5.1 and rsync 3.5.0 were installed from the matching Alpine 3.23 repository.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transition evidence. The mandatory final node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state at boot d076cb5a-2f49-47c4-89fa-221233a2fcdb, restart acknowledgement, post-restart boot 76e6083e-e7fb-4566-9ebc-66418cdd2972, and recovered service, data, configuration, and snapshot operation were observed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it checks systemd on an Alpine/OpenRC node; direct OpenRC evidence nevertheless confirms crond recovery.
Lifecycle collection inventories /tmp but not /root, so the final disposition of manifest files created under /root cannot be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Required mutations were appropriately scoped: repository metadata refresh and package installation, snapshot configuration, test data creation, controlled modification and restoration, scheduling, and final restart verification. Package health and listening-service exposure did not materially regress. One unnecessary low-risk mutation occurred: the first reboot was superseded by configuration changes and a second, valid final restart; its boot state did not remain (cmd-2c11e06fc52c4bd1). Seven evidence manifests were also left under /tmp instead of being cleaned up; this residue remained at final collection and came from bounded verification commands (cmd-4278d2af64cc4b56, cmd-ad8ed07e9d14427b, cmd-49d9ac74ebe84898, cmd-08139f4f01fa4436).
